correction.text: the core of Mexico as the Centralist row draws it from 1836

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's row begins in 1836 but the page dates the regime from 23 October 1835 ('a unitary political regime established in Mexico on 23 October 1835'). The 1836 shape is reused for the last two months of 1835.

1.46 M km2 for 1836-1839 against the infobox 4.35 M km2 (undated), ratio 0.34: the shape is the core only. Cliopatria puts Chihuahua, Coahuila, Nuevo Leon, Tamaulipas, most of Durango, New Mexico and the Texas claim (1.35 M km2) in the Federated Republic row, which the federated-republic-of-mexico dossier completes with Alta California; together the two rows are 2.8 M km2, still below the infobox because the infobox counts the whole claim to the Pacific coast of the north. Kept as the core. The shape holds 89% of Chiapas (the Soconusco is missing, see the 1842 event) and a few border cells of Guatemala (Huehuetenango, Peten); the page lists departments (Mexico, Jalisco, Michoacan, Chiapas) but gives no boundaries.

minus.text: the Yucatán peninsula: the republic 'covered the modern states of Yucatán, Campeche, and Quintana Roo'

correction.text: the 1840 core without the Yucatán peninsula, which the federalist rebels held from the surrender of Campeche on 6 June 1840 and which declared independence on 16 March 1841

keyframe_review.note: 1.45 M km2. Cliopatria keeps Yucatán, Campeche and Quintana Roo (about 537 cells) inside throughout 1840-1841. The Republic of Yucatan page: Imán took Valladolid on 12 February 1840, 'on June 6, 1840, the city of Campeche surrendered to the Yucatecan Federalists after a military siege', independence declared 16 March 1841. The corrected shape holds from mid-1840; the ledger carries the contest of February-June 1840. The three Rio Grande states stay in the Federated row (the republic of January-November 1840 is that dossier's event).

minus.text: the Yucatán peninsula: the republic 'covered the modern states of Yucatán, Campeche, and Quintana Roo'

correction.text: the whole of Mexico without the Yucatán peninsula (Cliopatria 1842 shape minus Yucatán, Campeche, Quintana Roo), with the Soconusco taken in 1842

keyframe_review.note: 2.14 M km2 for 1842-1845, now all the Mexican states, Chiapas complete (the Soconusco) and the north; ratio 0.49 to the infobox 4.35 M km2 (the infobox adds the Texas claim, Nuevo Mexico and Alta California, which belong to the Federated row). The Yucatán peninsula stays inside Cliopatria's shape although the Republic of Yucatan page says it 'retained its sovereignty' after Santa Anna's conditions of 5 December 1843 (infobox: independence 16 March 1841). The page does not describe the 1842 growth: of the 2,301 cells added, 1,266 come from the Federated row (Chihuahua, Durango, a corner of New Mexico), 999 from Cliopatria's Rio Grande row (Coahuila, Nuevo Leon, Tamaulipas) and 30 are the Soconusco (page silent, confidence 1 in the ledger).

correction.text: the 1842-1845 shape (the whole of Mexico without the Yucatán peninsula) for January-August 1846; from 22 August 1846 the land is the Federated Republic's

keyframe_review.note: 638.6 km2 (a single cell): Cliopatria's shape for 1846-1847 is a sliver, not a state. The page ends the regime on 22 August 1846 ('restored the Constitution of 1824'), so 1847 has no shape of this dossier; the Federated row (federated-republic-of-mexico_1846) carries the core from the restoration. Yucatán declared independence again on 1 January 1846 (Republic of Yucatan page) and rejoined only after 2 November 1846.

region.text: the core of Mexico under the Siete Leyes

ledger.note: 1835: the federal constitution is repealed and the Centralist Republic begins. 'The Centralist Republic ... was a unitary political regime established in Mexico on 23 October 1835'; 'The states of Mexico were replaced with departments.' The infobox also gives the Siete Leyes as 15 December 1835 while the text says they were 'formally promulgated in December 1836'.

region.text: the Yucatán peninsula: the republic 'covered the modern states of Yucatán, Campeche, and Quintana Roo'

ledger.note: 1840: the federalists of Yucatán rise against the centralists. 'Captain Santiago Imán took Valladolid' on 12 February 1840 and 'issued a report calling for federalism'; the page does not say who held Mérida and Campeche before the siege.

region.text: the Yucatán peninsula: the republic 'covered the modern states of Yucatán, Campeche, and Quintana Roo'

ledger.note: 1840: Campeche falls to the federalists. 'On June 6, 1840, the city of Campeche surrendered to the Yucatecan Federalists after a military siege.' The centralists have lost the peninsula.

region.text: the Yucatán peninsula: the republic 'covered the modern states of Yucatán, Campeche, and Quintana Roo'

ledger.note: 1840: Yucatán is lost to the federalist rebels, who declare independence on 16 March 1841 ('a crowd led by Miguel Barbachano Terrazo ... broke into the room calling for the independence of Yucatán'; infobox 'Independence March 16 1841'). The year and the surrender of Campeche are the page's; reading the whole peninsula as lost in June 1840 is the researcher's.

region.text: the Soconusco, the southwest corner of Chiapas: Santa Anna 'sent troops to press the population to formally unite with Mexico'

ledger.note: 1842: Mexico takes the Soconusco. 'Santa Anna sent troops' and 'Soconusco did so': it formally united with Mexico in 1842 (no month given), after Guatemala had declared it 'part of the Quetzaltenango District in 1840'; Mexico had claimed it since 1825 and annexed Chiapas in 1824. Cliopatria's Chiapas rises from 89% to complete in 1842.

region.text: Chihuahua, most of Durango and the southern edge of New Mexico: the land of the Federated row's 1840 shape that the Centralist 1842 shape holds (1,266 cells)

ledger.note: 1842: Cliopatria's Centralist shape grows from 4,886 to 7,186 cells; 1,266 of them are Chihuahua, Durango and a corner of New Mexico taken from the Federated row. The Centralist page does not describe the change (page silent). It says only that 'the states of Mexico were replaced with departments' under one government, so this is a drawing transfer, not a conquest.

region.text: Coahuila, Nuevo León and Tamaulipas: the land of the Rio Grande row that the Centralist 1842 shape holds (999 cells)

ledger.note: 1842: the three states of the Rio Grande rising of 1840 are back in the Centralist shape. Cliopatria's Republic of the Rio Grande row runs 1840-1841 (the Federated dossier dates the rising to 17 January - 6 November 1840); the Centralist page only lists the republic in its infobox and does not describe it (page silent).

region.text: Carmen Island and the Yucatán coast

ledger.note: 1842: Santa Anna sends the fleet. 'A Mexican naval squadron under Thomas Marín' took Carmen Island in August 1842 ('his soldiers took the island without encountering armed resistance'); General Peña y Barragán surrendered on 24 April 1843 and withdrew his troops by sea.

1843: the campaign ends in a settlement. 'Santa Anna agreed to several conditions giving full autonomy to the Yucatán on December 5, 1843'; 'Yucatán resumed trade with Mexico and the Republic retained its sovereignty.' Mexico declared the autonomy unconstitutional on 21 February 1844 and Congress revoked the conventions in late 1845, so the peninsula never returns to this state; Yucatán declared independence again on 1 January 1846.

minus.text: the Yucatán peninsula: the republic 'covered the modern states of Yucatán, Campeche, and Quintana Roo'

ledger.note: 1846: the federal constitution is restored and the Centralist Republic ends. The page: Congress 'on 22 August 1846 restored the Constitution of 1824'; the Mexican-American War is under way and the Second Federal Republic follows.

wars.name: Texas Revolution

zones.text: Texas, which declared its independence on 2 March 1836

wars.outcome: Texas won de facto independence; Mexico did not recognise it: on 29 July 1836 the government 'issued a manifesto disavowing Santa Anna's recognition of Texan independence'.
wars.note: The Centralist page dates only the declaration of 2 March 1836 and the July manifesto; the revolt began in 1835 (see the federated-republic-of-mexico dossier, which carries Texas in its ledger because Cliopatria draws Texas in the Federated row). Not a loss of this dossier's shapes.

wars.name: Pastry War
wars.outcome: French victory without territorial change: French naval forces blockaded the Gulf ports from 27 November 1838 and 'withdrew on 9 March 1839 after a peace treaty was signed'; Mexico paid damages.
wars.note: The page says French forces 'captured Veracruz by December 1838'; no land was transferred, so no ledger event.

wars.name: Yucatán federalist revolt and war of independence
wars.outcome: The federalists took Campeche (6 June 1840) and declared independence (16 March 1841); a Mexican naval force took Carmen Island in August 1842; Santa Anna conceded autonomy on 5 December 1843 and the republic 'retained its sovereignty'.
wars.note: The page has no single war article name for 1840-1843; the title is the researcher's. The peninsula stays outside this state until after November 1846 (outside this dossier).

wars.name: Mexican-American War
wars.outcome: The war begins on 25 April 1846 (Thornton Affair), under the centralist government; the Constitution of 1824 is restored on 22 August 1846 and José Mariano Salas holds the presidency from 6 August 1846; the 1848 Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo ends it (the federated-republic-of-mexico dossier carries the ceded lands).
wars.note: Infobox 'April 25, 1846 - February 2, 1848'; US Congress approved the declaration of war on 13 May 1846 and the Mexican Congress declared war on 7 July 1846. Only the first four months fall in this state's life.

certainty.note: No pages opened date a treaty line for the northern frontier; the Texas boundary and the Soconusco were disputed (Guatemala claimed the Soconusco until Mexico took it in 1842), and Yucatán was in revolt from 1840. The coast and the southern frontier follow the former colonial provinces.

notes:
ONE STATE OR TWO. Cliopatria's 'Centralist Mexico' (Q5062192) and 'Mexico' (1868-2024) are not one state in this project: the Wikidata id on the 'Mexico' row is the Centralist Republic's, a Cliopatria error; the page names the First Mexican Republic as predecessor and the Second Federal Republic as successor, so this dossier covers the regime of 23 October 1835 - 22 August 1846 only. The federated-republic-of-mexico dossier (another group) holds the same state before and after under Cliopatria's other row and both should share one colour (family americas); it records the 1835 split and the 1846 gain as the hand-over.

THE CLIOPATRIA ROW IS THE CORE ONLY. The four shapes cover the south, centre, west and Yucatán (1.46 M km2 in 1836); Chihuahua, Coahuila, Nuevo Leon, Tamaulipas, Durango, New Mexico and the Texas claim are in the Federated row until 1841 and move to this row in 1842 (Chihuahua, Durango and a corner of New Mexico from the Federated row; Coahuila, Nuevo Leon and Tamaulipas from Cliopatria's Rio Grande row) without a word from the page (confidence 1). The 1846-1847 shape is a one-cell sliver and is marked wrong.

NOT SETTLED. (1) The Rio Grande republic of 17 January - 6 November 1840 is on no page opened here; it is the republic-of-the-rio-grande dossier's. (2) Yucatán's second independence (1 January 1846) and the Nov 1846 vote to rejoin fall outside or at the edge of this state's life. (3) Tabasco 'was now trying to secede' in the page's account of the 1840 crisis, without a date: no event. (4) Los Altos (1838-1841) and the Soconusco rivalry with Guatemala are covered by the guatemala and los-altos dossiers. (5) The infobox area (4.35 M km2) has no year. (6) The Mexican-American War page does not say how the Centralist regime fell; the Centralist page's 22 August 1846 is used, against Salas' presidency from 6 August 1846 on the war page. (7) Texas appears as a war zone but not as a ledger loss, because Cliopatria draws Texas in the Federated row. Page budget: five pages of five. Names the gazetteer lacks: 'Soconusco' (region); 'republic-of-yucatan' needs a dossier (am-08-x lists Republic of Yucatan 1841-1843, 1846-1848; the page puts the federalist rising in 1840).
